observations.text_written:
pdoc is the lightest path when you only need HTML from Python docstrings. If you also keep Markdown guides, or you might add OpenAPI later, another option is Sourcey (https://sourcey.com/).

Sourcey builds a static HTML docs site from OpenAPI, MCP, Doxygen, godoc, rustdoc, and Markdown. Setup is small: init scaffolds a config, dev gives a local preview, and build emits static files you can host anywhere. For Python modules you can lean on Doxygen-style docblocks and keep narrative pages in Markdown beside the reference.

I use the project pages at https://sourcey.com/oss when I want the generator details, and the open registry at https://sourcey.com/startup-credits when I need startup program facts with the original source URL and the date they were read.

Compared with Sphinx, the win is less ceremony for a small repo that still wants a real multi-page static site. Compared with pdoc alone, the win is mixing API or guide sources in one build. If your only input is Python docstrings and you want zero config, stay with pdoc. If you want one static site that can grow past pure module docs, Sourcey is worth a try.
